item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.content:encoded:
Hello Pumgumgum! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

SCP-XXXX is a script
SCP-XXXX embeds itself in online multiplayer games
SCP-XXXX is uneditable or deletable
SCP-XXXX generates a fictitious user account: SCP-XXXX-1
SCP-XXXX-1 always possesses the same username
SCP-XXXX-1 is mostly in-active (or AFK), but will randomly enter short “active” states
During “active” states, SCP-XXXX-1 is capable of communication and seems to innately know each players interests. Having conversations about said topics.
Players who interact with SCP-XXXX-1 will develop a desire to frequent and talk with it, claiming “he is fun to talk to” and “he understands me”.
Players will start prioritising surveying SCP-XXXX-1 for it’s next “active” state over important self needs, such as, consumption of victuals, socialising, sleep, etc.
Players will show signs of stress and violence when deprived of contact with SCP-XXXX-1.
Players exposed for longer than 100 hours will express dysphoria
SCP-XXXX-1 has yet to kill or influence the death of any victim, but can inflict heavy irreversible physical and psychological damage.

While the concept sounds doable, there isn't much on its purpose or what its end goal is. The skip doesn't seem to aiming for anything particular, which makes the concept (and the narrative to an extent) feel a bit flat/directionless to me.

The narrative:
As for the narrative;

There doesn't really seem to be a clear progression shown here, the structure of the article is laid out (which at this point I would really say is necessary). But the actual events and characters aren't really covered in enough detail to get invested emotionally (or become invested in the skip). Currently the narrative just sort of says there are interviews, or says who the characters are, but there isn't anything showing what they actually learn or what everything is building up to. whats the main conflict? what will make me invested in the characters?-what is their main arc and how do they change? whats the payoff? how will all of this make me as the reader feel?

Quickly noting; its a bit odd how the Foundation found the skip so easily, it doesn't really sound like they had any real way to know if the skip was anomalous, with no prior information.-its a quiet subtle if you don't look in the right places.

Red or green?
Due to may fore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.content:encoded:
Noting a PM request to take yet another look

This definitely elaborates on the character of -1 in a more in-depth way; but it still feels…narratively very flat? Like, as a story centred around -1, they don't grow in any manner or change over the course of the story, or face any adversity that they're forced to try and overcome; but it also feels like the focus on -1 might be a mistake on some level too: the Foundation are like, your PoV characters here and so it's often easier to write something framed around the Foundation interacting with the SCP. There's often a tendency for the conflict to then be centred around the Foundation and the SCP wanting/needing/doing things that are incompatible; and it feels like really considering what the purpose of their interactions is here would help. Considering the emotional reactions can be really helpful too: if you have an idea of how you want the reader to feel about e.g. -1 and the Foundation's treatment of it, you can start to figure out what the Foundation has to do to inspire that reaction.

So, I guess my tl;dr is: you're writing a story here but you've still gotta figure out the central conflict of the story, and how the characters within it change (either by choice or because they're forced to by the events of the story).

Noting a PM request to take another look

You've, definitely sort of tightened this up so it feels more cohesive as a whole; but it also feels very…flat? I don't really have an idea of like, what you're intending to do with the actual narrative or how the like, situation changes over the course of the story, or what the stakes are or anything. item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.content:encoded:
I'm not really a fan of an idea that boils actual addictions down to 'oh it's an anomaly', particularly ones that can be as quietly harmful to people as video game addictions can be.

Beyond this, the narrative feels…unfocussed? It kinda flits around various ideas: the behavioural patterns of the SCP, the way it affects players, the list of games it was part of; and it feels like these ideas never really come together to form a single, cohesive whole. It also feels like this could really do with a like…single affected player as the focus character, like, someone we can see slipping into worse and worse patterns of behaviour and whose plight is empathetic in a way that fills us with dread as we see them descend towards some final outcome that's terrible; but my concern is that the effect of the SCP is too compulsive for this to work well. That is to say: the SCP is effectively forcing them to become addicted, so there's no real like, choice or ability for them to like resist this or anything; whereas if the SCP was more…'seductive', then you can really like, have them be conflicted about whether they should stop and really give the narrative the conflict it needs that way.

I don't think it necessarily needs to be focussed in this specific manner; but it does feel like it all needs to come together in a way that makes it feel like this is telling a single, coherent story and it doesn't quite yet do that, for me.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.content:encoded:
A seemingly insignificant script which mysteriously appears in popular online multiplayers, generates a user account of which in game exposure can influence the mind.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is a script
  • SCP-XXXX embeds itself in online multiplayer games
  • SCP-XXXX is uneditable or deletable
  • SCP-XXXX generates a fictitious user account: SCP-XXXX-1
  • SCP-XXXX-1 always possesses the same username
  • SCP-XXXX-1 is mostly in-active (or AFK), but will randomly enter short “active” states
  • During “active” states, SCP-XXXX-1 is capable of communication and seems to innately know each players interests. Having conversations about said topics.
  • Players who interact with SCP-XXXX-1 will develop a desire to frequent and talk with it, claiming “he is fun to talk to” and “he understands me”.
  • Players will start prioritising surveying SCP-XXXX-1 for it’s next “active” state over important self needs, such as, consumption of victuals, socialising, sleep, etc.
  • Players will show signs of stress and violence when deprived of contact with SCP-XXXX-1.
  • Players exposed for longer than 100 hours will express dysphoria
  • SCP-XXXX-1 has yet to kill or influence the death of any victim, but can inflict heavy irreversible physical and psychological damage.

Central Narrative: This article will be written according to the standard layout: starting with containment procedures, a description and finishing with an addendum. Using professional language with clinical wording, to give the article a sense of authenticity.

Containment procedures will outline both monitoring instructions for the host game ( including a cover-up story for participating publishing companies) and containment deals with SCP-XXXX-1. Procedures for interviews {SCP-XXXX seems to only switch games in order to find new individuals for SCP-XXXX-1 to manipulate. Hence, an accord has been set with SCP-XXXX-1, wherein new users (D-class personnel) are to be presented to SCP-XXXX-1 on a regular basis and in return SCP-XXXX-1 does not go looking for individuals nor will SCP-XXXX change game. A new development in SCP-XXXX-1’s behavior, as he normally only does as he wishes, but now, seems to apply himself to another’s rules - in response to cybersqyd}. How players coming into "contact" with SCP-XXXX-1 are to be dealt with.

The description will briefly detail SCP-XXXX’s nature and odd properties, but will focus more heavily on SCP-XXXX-1. How, it is a sly talker who seduces players into frequenting it, theories about it’s intentions and goals, small pieces of interviews with SCP-XXXX-1 and information it refuses to disclose {SCP-XXXX-1 is a manipulative entity who dupes victims into desiring it’s attention. Using techniques such as: common interests, empathy, comedy, pity and curiosity. Trapping players into a vicious circle of seeking out it’s recognition. It is unknown if SCP-XXXX-1 does this out of need or for pleasure. - response to cybersqyd}.

The addendum will feature a report of SCP-XXXX’s discovery, by Dr. [placeholder] {Dr. [Placeholder] will be used as the reader’s gateway into the piece. As a human character recording SCP-XXXX for the first time, the reader may identify as Dr. [Placeholder] and experience the changes he goes through - in response to cybersqyd} his journey from a respectable foundation team leader to a decrepit sad childish antisocial shadow of his former self (eventually relegated) {the character of Dr. [Placeholder] is to be curious yet serious, as a professional researcher at the foundation. Slowly, however, reports drafted by him will become increasingly biased towards SCP-XXXX-1 and “nonclinical”. Eventually, reports will be written by other members of staff, due to Dr. [Placeholder] no longer willing, nor being fit, to write them. The final report will be a relegation order to D-class, after failed attempts to rehabilitate Dr. [Placeholder]. - in response to cybersqyd}. This aims to illustrate an interaction with SCP-XXXX-1 and the extent of the damage it can cause.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article seeks to create a fictitious origin for extreme IAD (Internet addiction disorder). In addition, this article is inspired by the collective input of the ChilloutVR community, by an inside joke/meme of this very SCP joked to be the source of users who spend their lives in virtual reality (and by extension any other online multiplayers).
